# Automatic differentiation is a testing problem

## Nobody can tell you which backend to use

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Six configurations in CI. ForwardDiff, ReverseDiff on tape, Enzyme
  forward and reverse, Mooncake forward and reverse
- Each gets its own job, its own badge and its own Codecov flag, so you
  can see which lines a backend actually reaches
- `CensoredDistributions.jl` is green on all six. It is green because
  two Enzyme scenarios are declared broken and tracked as an issue
- `ComposedDistributions.jl` fails all six on `main` today
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-important}
DifferentiationInterface tells you about a function. Turing tells you
what Turing tests. Nothing tells you about a model assembled from five
packages that each tested on their own.
:::

- The one public per-backend table for a probabilistic programming
  stack, `TuringLang/ADTests`, was archived in June 2026
:::
::::

## What we added on top of DifferentiationInterfaceTest

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- DifferentiationInterfaceTest is the right tool and we use it. It works
  per function and per package
- We added a registry where a package declares which scenarios are
  broken on which backend, and `check_broken` re-runs them, so a broken
  scenario that starts passing gets flagged rather than left stale
- One list generates the CI matrix, the Codecov flags, the README badges
  and the published support table, so the docs cannot drift from CI
- `EpiAwareADTools.jl` holds the workarounds. `gamma_inc` and `beta_inc`
  are not differentiable, so we hand-wrote those derivatives
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-important}
Mooncake returned a wrong gradient for a Gamma shape at `shape == 1`.
Not an error. A wrong number.
:::

- Every workaround is documented against the upstream issue that should
  delete it. It is a staging ground, not a feature
- `ScoringRules.jl` hit the same two functions from scratch

::: {.attribution}
Without this, building a model is a custom job with a lot of iteration.
That is not realistic in an outbreak.
:::
:::
::::
